sources.title: Breaking the Tragedy of the Horizon – climate change and financial stability
sources.venue: Bank of England (speech at Lloyd's of London)
sources.quote_checked: Climate change is the Tragedy of the Horizon. | We don't need an army of actuaries to tell us that the catastrophic impacts of climate change will be felt beyond the traditional horizons of most actors | once climate change becomes a defining issue for financial stability, it may already be too late | By managing what gets measured, we can break the Tragedy of the Horizon.

sources.title: The Reith Lectures 2020: From Climate Crisis to Real Prosperity
sources.quote_checked: that's a striking gap between what society wants and what the market values | the market is not the answer to everything, but it can play a critical role | We won't get to net zero without innovation, investment and profit.

sources.title: Principled and Pragmatic: Canada's Path
sources.quote_checked: Middle powers must act together because if you are not at the table, you are on the menu. | when we only negotiate bilaterally with a hegemon, we negotiate from weakness. | This is not sovereignty. It is the performance of sovereignty while accepting subordination. | sovereignty that was once grounded in rules, but will increasingly be anchored in the ability to withstand pressure | They must develop greater strategic autonomy: in energy, food, critical minerals, in finance, and supply chains.
